dedupe_keys.name: small accessible urban parks and heat related mortality in 265 chinese cities nature health 2026

description: This study asks which spatial patterns of urban green space best reduce heatwave deaths, using daily mortality in 265 Chinese cities and five landscape metrics of green space. Researchers from Fudan University, the Chinese Center for Disease Control and Prevention and Helmholtz Munich published it in Nature Health on 15 January 2026. Coverage is 265 cities across China. The heatwave mortality risk was higher where green space was scarce or aggregated into few large patches: for heatwaves at or above the 92.5th percentile lasting at least two days, the relative risk was 1.11 at a low share of green space against 1.04 at a high share, and similar gaps appear for fragmentation and shape complexity, pointing to many small, accessible parks. Format and access: an article with code on GitHub; green space comes from the EULUC-China land use map. Licence: the mortality data from China CDC are not public, so the analysis cannot be fully rerun; the article licence was not read. Caveats: it is an ecological city-level study. It gives effect sizes for climate adaptation and exposure models that treat parks as heat-protective green infrastructure. A related catalogue record is the global urban heat island heatwave exposure data set.
